intro: School and university words, with several that look like English and mean something else.
p.la carrera.nota: In an academic context, a course of university studies. It can also mean a race or a person's professional career.
p.la asignatura: the school or university subject; course unit
p.matricularse.nota: Usually followed by en: matricularse en una asignatura or en un grado.
p.el instituto.nota: In Spain, often a state secondary school. ESO is normally for ages 12–16; some institutes also offer optional Bachillerato, usually ages 16–18.
p.hacer prácticas: to do a work placement; internship
p.el colegio.nota: In Spain, often a primary school. It does not mean a university college.
p.el grado.nota: Most Spanish official Grado programmes have 240 ECTS credits (four academic years); some have 300 or 360.
p.el bachillerato.nota: In Spain, an optional two-year stage, normally for ages 16–18.
p.aprobado.nota: As a grade label, aprobado means a pass; the adjective agrees with the noun.
p.notable.nota: In the usual university grading scale, notable is a grade from 7 to 8.9 out of 10.
p.sobresaliente.nota: In the usual university grading scale, sobresaliente is a grade from 9 to 10 out of 10.
p.sacar un ocho: to get a mark of eight
p.asistir a clase.nota: Asistir a means to attend; asistir does not mean to help in this phrase.
b1.titulo: The system and its false friends
b1.texto:
In Spain, children usually attend primary school at **el colegio**. Compulsory secondary education (**ESO**) normally runs from ages 12 to 16, often at **el instituto**. **Bachillerato** is optional and usually for ages 16 to 18. At university, many students enrol in **un grado**; most degrees have 240 ECTS credits (four academic years), though some are longer. They may continue with **un máster** or **un doctorado**.

University marks use a 0–10 scale: below 5 is **suspenso**; **aprobado** is 5–6.9, **notable** 7–8.9 and **sobresaliente** 9–10.

Useful verbs: **hacer un examen** (sit/take an exam), **aprobar**, **suspender**, **sacar un ocho**, **repasar** and **tomar apuntes**.

Some words can mislead English speakers: **la carrera** is a degree course or programme, not necessarily a professional career; **el colegio** means school, not college; **la asignatura** is a course subject, while **el sujeto** is a grammatical subject; **suspender** an exam means to fail it; **asistir a clase** means to attend class, not to help.
b2.f1: I've passed everything except one subject. I've failed Statistics.
b2.f2: What a pity! And what mark did you get in History?
b2.f3: A nine. If I get good marks, they'll give me the scholarship.
b2.f4: When you finish your degree, will you do a master's degree?
b2.f5: First I want to do a work placement at a company.
b4.o1.explicacion: Suspender an exam is to fail it.
b5.pregunta: For a university student, «la carrera» is…
b6.o1.refuerzo: Spanish does not take a mark.
b6.o2.refuerzo: Hacer goes with the exam itself.
b7.pregunta: Complete: when you finish your degree, will you travel?
b7.o0.refuerzo: A future cuando takes the subjunctive.
b8.o0.refuerzo: ESO is normally for ages 12–16; Bachillerato is optional and usually 16–18.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That would be un centro de investigación.
b9.traduccion: If I get good marks, they'll give me the scholarship.
b10.o0.refuerzo: Asistir a means to be present at a class.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Faltar a clase means to miss class.
b11.pregunta: Which word means a school or university subject?
b11.o2.refuerzo: A university degree course or programme.

**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Write about your education: what you studied, what you would study now and why.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Tell aloud about the most difficult exam of your life.
